L9:     Abstract
L10: 
L11:        This document proposes an additional endpoint for OAuth authorization
L12:        servers, which allows clients to notify the authorization server that
L13:        a previously obtained refresh or access token is no longer needed.
L14:        This allows the authorization server to clean up security
L15:        credentials.  A revocation request will invalidate the actual token
L16:        and, if applicable, other tokens based on the same authorization
L17:        grant.

L111:     【5†1】.  Introduction
L112: 
L113:        The OAuth 2.0 core specification [【33†RFC6749】] defines several ways for a
L114:        client to obtain refresh and access tokens.  This specification
L115:        supplements the core specification with a mechanism to revoke both
L116:        types of tokens.  A token is a string representing an authorization
L117:        grant issued by the resource owner to the client.  A revocation
L118:        request will invalidate the actual token and, if applicable, other
L119:        tokens based on the same authorization grant and the authorization
L120:        grant itself.
L121: 
L122:        From an end-user's perspective, OAuth is often used to log into a
L123:        certain site or application.  This revocation mechanism allows a
L124:        client to invalidate its tokens if the end-user logs out, changes
L125:        identity, or uninstalls the respective application.  Notifying the
L126:        authorization server that the token is no longer needed allows the
L127:        authorization server to clean up data associated with that token
L128:        (e.g., session data) and the underlying authorization grant.  This
L129:        behavior prevents a situation in which there is still a valid
L130:        authorization grant for a particular client of which the end-user is
L131:        not aware.  This way, token revocation prevents abuse of abandoned
L132:        tokens and facilitates a better end-user experience since invalidated
L133:        authorization grants will no longer turn up in a list of
L134:        authorization grants the authorization server might present to the
L135:        end-user.
L136: 
L137:     【7†1.1】.  Requirements Language
L138: 
L139:        The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT",
L140:        "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this
L141:        document are to be interpreted as described in 【34†RFC 2119】 [【34†RFC2119】].
L142: 
L143:     【8†2】.  Token Revocation
L144: 
L145:        Implementations MUST support the revocation of refresh tokens and
L146:        SHOULD support the revocation of access tokens (see Implementation
L147:        Note).
